text:
The reigning Hart Trophy winner is playing every night under a headline. NHL Trade Rumors reported this week that Nikita Kucherov's agent says the split with the Lightning is beyond repair, and Sportsnet is already sorting through landing spots. The team's own video calls him the "Franchise All-Time Leading Scorer," and he may be skating out his time there.

On the ice, his season is quieter than his reputation and less worrying than it looks. He has 20 points in 15 games but only 4 goals, none in his last six. He's shooting 9.8%; our talent range puts him nearer 15%. The chances are about where they should be (5.0 expected goals), and Tampa owns 58% of the five-on-five expected goals with him on. That's a finishing dip, not a decline.

Evolving-Hockey ranked him second among all forwards in 2025-26, with one caveat: opponents' chances rose with him on the ice, bottom 11% among forwards. Whoever ends up with him, if anyone does, gets a player whose goals are due back. Our projection still puts him in the 124-point neighborhood.
headline: Playing under a headline in Tampa
